narr: From the July 4th weekend into the early part of the following week, a weak upper trough lingered over North and Central Texas, triggering several days of scattered showers and thunderstorms. A saturated atmosphere combined with slow storm motions resulted in numerous flash flooding events throughout the region, particularly in Central Texas.
ev: A trained spotter reported that flood waters were obstructing multiple lanes of Loop 12 in Irving.
County dispatch relayed a report of multiple spots of water over the road on FM 1602 in eastern Hamilton County.
Coryell County dispatch reported that the road was impassable due to flooding in the 6000 block of FM 217 near Turnersville.
A social media video indicated running water over County Road 906 east of Godley.
The Somervell County Emergency Manager reported a vehicle stuck in high water on FM 202 southeast of Glen Rose.
Emergency management reported that FM 56 near Brazos Point was closed due to water over the road.
Fire and rescue reported 2 water rescues in Stephenville, with evacuations underway in one neighborhood as of this report.
Comanche County Dispatch reported that County Road 434 near Proctor Lake (west of the town of Proctor) was impassible due to flood waters.
Comanche County Dispatch reported that County Road 420 was closed near Proctor Lake due to flood waters.

A news media article reported multiple roads closed in Killeen due to flooding. Streets included Stallion Drive, Tiger Lane, Woodrow Drive, Alleeta St, Bunny Trail, Tatonka Dr, Bachelor Button Blvd, Watercrest Road, and Willow Springs Road.
A social media report indicated flooded roads near Lindsey Drive and Jesse Drive in Copperas Cove.
Emergency management reported that County Road 3300 was shut down near Kempner due to flooding.
Emergency management reported that County Road 3100 just west of Brooks Crossing was shut down due to flooding.
Emergency management reported roads inundated at and around High Street and Delphine Street in Terrell. At least one car had water up to the hood in the picture that was provided.
TXDOT reported that FM 575 was closed between FM 2005 and County Road 262 northwest of Goldthwaite due to flood waters.
Law enforcement reported that County Road 218 southwest of Cameron was closed due to flooding.
Law enforcement reported that County Road 134 located of north of Ben Arnold was closed due to flooding.
Broadcast media produced a video of vehicles stalled on north Dallas at West-Northwest Highway near Hillcrest due to about 6 inches of water on the road.
Emergency management reported that stranded motorists were extracted from flood waters near Military Parkway and Scyene Road in Mesquite.
Dispatch reported that FM 1602 and Hwy 22 near Lanham had water over the road.
County dispatch reported that County Road 513 near the intersection of County Road 518 south of Shive was impassible due to flooding.
Emergency management reported that FM 216 north of Iredell was closed at 10 AM due to water over the road.
Emergency management reported that County Road 915 near the intersection of County Road 1014 northwest of Joshua was closed due to flooding.

Amateur radio reported an area of impacted or closed roads due to high water between Copperas Cove and Pidcoke, including Cactus Lane at Wagon Wheel, West Avenue B from North 11th to Northern Dove Lane, and Summers Road at Ashley Drive.

Emergency management confirmed that multiple roads in Copperas Cove had become impassable due to flooding, with vehicles stranded on these roadways, primarily in residential areas on the north side of town.
Emergency management reported a swift water rescue in the 1100 block of Indian Trail at a low water crossing, just southeast of McGregor.
